title: adj guard check: flag a client passed as an argument or bound with `var`, and an inverted guard

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Raised by the reviewer in round 1 of ork run ork-20261125-235639-7e56 for S570 (discovered from S570):

adj guard check: flag a client passed as an argument or bound with `var`, and an inverted guard
My probe (TestProbeEdges, temp dir) ran the checker on edge cases. It flagged the else branch (`17: elseBranch`) and the goroutine literal (`22: lit`). It did not flag three forms:
- `use(e.d.Adj)`, the client passed as an argument;
- `var c = e.d.Adj`;
- `if e.proj.Adj { return }` followed by `e.d.Adj.Check`, an inverted guard that passes as guarded.
The slice's definition of a client use (Implement 3) leaves the first two out, and its early-exit rule accepts the third, so none of them is a defect in this slice. None of these forms occurs in the engine today.
